title: The Great Pyramid of Giza is finished
blurb: Egyptian workers stacked over two million blocks of stone. It stayed the tallest building on Earth for about 3,800 years.

title: Hammurabi carves his laws into stone
blurb: The Babylonian king had 282 laws chiselled onto a tall pillar so everyone could see the rules. It is one of the oldest written law codes we still have.

title: Tutankhamun becomes pharaoh of Egypt
blurb: He was about nine years old. He ruled for roughly ten years and died as a teenager.

title: The first Olympic Games are held in Greece
blurb: One race, about 190 metres long. The prize was a wreath of olive leaves, not a medal.

title: Socrates is put on trial in Athens
blurb: The philosopher was accused of corrupting young minds by asking too many awkward questions. He was sentenced to death.

title: Alexander the Great becomes king
blurb: He was 20. Within thirteen years he had conquered an empire stretching from Greece to India.

title: Qin Shi Huang unites China
blurb: He became China's first emperor and standardised the writing, money and even the width of cart axles.

title: Julius Caesar is assassinated in Rome
blurb: Roman senators feared he was becoming a king. His death helped turn the Roman Republic into an empire.

title: Mount Vesuvius buries Pompeii
blurb: Ash covered the Roman town so fast that loaves of bread were preserved in the ovens.
wiki: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

title: Cai Lun improves papermaking in China
blurb: He mashed bark, rags and old fishing nets into pulp. Cheap paper meant far more people could write things down.

title: The Western Roman Empire falls
blurb: The last emperor in Rome was pushed off the throne. The eastern half carried on for another thousand years.
wiki: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

title: Muhammad journeys from Mecca to Medina
blurb: This journey, the Hijra, is year one of the Islamic calendar.

title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
blurb: The pope placed a crown on him on Christmas Day, making him ruler of much of western Europe.

title: Leif Erikson reaches North America
blurb: Norse sailors landed in what is now Canada, roughly 500 years before Columbus crossed the Atlantic.

title: The Battle of Hastings
blurb: William of Normandy defeated King Harold and took over England, changing its language forever.

title: Genghis Khan founds the Mongol Empire
blurb: It grew into the largest connected land empire in history, stretching from Korea to eastern Europe.

title: King John signs Magna Carta
blurb: English barons forced the king to agree he was not above the law. The idea stuck.

title: Marco Polo sets out for China
blurb: The teenage Venetian travelled for 24 years. His book about it inspired later explorers, including Columbus.

title: The Black Death reaches Europe
blurb: The plague killed perhaps a third of everyone in Europe within a few years.

title: Joan of Arc is executed
blurb: A teenage farm girl who led French armies against the English. Twenty-five years later the verdict against her was overturned.

title: Gutenberg builds his printing press
blurb: Movable metal type made books cheap. Ideas could now spread across a continent in months instead of lifetimes.

title: Columbus reaches the Americas
blurb: He was looking for a sea route to Asia and insisted for years that he had found one.

title: Leonardo da Vinci starts the Mona Lisa
blurb: He kept tinkering with it for years and never handed it over to the man who ordered it.

title: Magellan's expedition sets sail
blurb: Five ships left Spain to sail all the way around the world. One ship and 18 men made it back three years later.

title: Copernicus says Earth orbits the Sun
blurb: His book was published as he lay dying. It took a century for most people to accept he was right.

title: Jamestown is founded in Virginia
blurb: The first lasting English settlement in North America. Most of the first colonists did not survive the early years.

title: Galileo points a telescope at the sky
blurb: He found mountains on the Moon and four moons circling Jupiter, proving not everything orbits Earth.

title: The Mayflower crosses the Atlantic
blurb: 102 passengers spent 66 days at sea in a ship built for cargo, not people.

title: The Great Fire of London
blurb: It started in a bakery and burned for four days, destroying most of the medieval city.

title: Newton publishes the Principia
blurb: One set of rules explained both a falling apple and an orbiting Moon. It is arguably the most important science book ever written.

title: The first hot air balloon flight
blurb: The Montgolfier brothers sent up a sheep, a duck and a rooster first, to check it was safe.

title: The US Declaration of Independence
blurb: Thirteen colonies announced they were no longer ruled by Britain. The war to prove it lasted seven more years.

title: The French Revolution begins
blurb: A crowd stormed the Bastille prison in Paris. Within four years France had no king at all.

title: The first steam locomotive runs on rails
blurb: Richard Trevithick's engine hauled ten tonnes of iron in Wales. Railways would soon shrink the world.

title: Gold is found in California
blurb: Around 300,000 people rushed west hoping to strike it rich. Most did not.

title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
blurb: His idea of evolution by natural selection explained why living things fit their surroundings so well.

title: The Emancipation Proclamation
blurb: President Lincoln declared enslaved people in the rebelling southern states to be free.

title: The Suez Canal opens
blurb: A shortcut between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea cut thousands of miles off the voyage to Asia.

title: Bell patents the telephone
blurb: His first words down the line were reportedly a request for his assistant to come into the room.

title: Edison makes a practical light bulb
blurb: The trick was not the idea but the filament. His team tested thousands of materials to find one that lasted.

title: Karl Benz builds the first car
blurb: A three-wheeled machine with a petrol engine. His wife Bertha took it on the first long drive to prove it worked.

title: New Zealand lets women vote
blurb: The first self-governing country in the world to do it. Other countries took decades to follow.

title: A radio signal crosses the Atlantic
blurb: Marconi sent three dots, the letter S, from England to Newfoundland. Experts had said the curve of the Earth made it impossible.

title: The Wright brothers fly
blurb: The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered 37 metres, shorter than a jumbo jet is long.

title: The Titanic sinks
blurb: The largest ship afloat hit an iceberg on its first voyage. There were lifeboats for only about half the people aboard.

title: World War One begins
blurb: A chain of alliances turned one assassination into a war across Europe that lasted four years.

title: American women win the vote
blurb: The 19th Amendment passed after more than seventy years of campaigning.
wiki: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: Tutankhamun's tomb is discovered
blurb: Howard Carter found it almost untouched after 3,000 years, packed with over 5,000 objects.

title: Fleming discovers penicillin
blurb: He left a dish out by accident and mould killed the bacteria growing on it. Antibiotics have saved millions of lives since.

title: The world's first regular TV service
blurb: The BBC began broadcasting to a few hundred sets in London. A television cost about as much as a small car.

title: World War Two begins
blurb: Germany invaded Poland and Britain and France declared war. It became the deadliest conflict in history.

title: World War Two ends
blurb: Fighting stopped in Europe in May and in the Pacific in September. The United Nations was founded the same year.

title: India becomes independent
blurb: After nearly 200 years of British rule, and a long campaign led in part by Gandhi's non-violent protest.

title: The shape of DNA is worked out
blurb: A twisted ladder, the double helix. Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images were essential to the discovery.
wiki: Discovery of the structure of DNA

title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her seat
blurb: Her arrest in Montgomery, Alabama sparked a bus boycott that lasted 381 days.

title: Sputnik becomes the first satellite
blurb: A metal sphere the size of a beach ball beeped as it circled Earth, and started the space race.

title: Yuri Gagarin is the first human in space
blurb: One orbit, 108 minutes. He was 27 years old.

title: Martin Luther King Jr's 'I Have a Dream'
blurb: He spoke to 250,000 people in Washington. The most famous part of the speech was improvised.

title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
blurb: Around 600 million people watched. The guidance computer had less power than a modern calculator.

title: The Voyager probes launch
blurb: They are still flying, now beyond our solar system, each carrying a golden record of sounds from Earth.

title: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster
blurb: A reactor test went wrong in Ukraine. The nearby city of Pripyat is still empty today.

title: The Berlin Wall falls
blurb: After 28 years splitting the city, crowds climbed over and began knocking it down with hammers.

title: The Hubble Space Telescope launches
blurb: Its mirror was ground slightly wrong, so astronauts flew up in 1993 to fit it with corrective optics.

title: The World Wide Web opens to everyone
blurb: Tim Berners-Lee put the first website online and gave the technology away for free.

title: Nelson Mandela is elected president
blurb: South Africa's first election where everyone could vote, four years after he left prison.

title: A computer beats the chess world champion
blurb: IBM's Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in a six-game match.

title: The first iPhone goes on sale
blurb: A phone with no keyboard. Within a decade most of the planet was carrying a computer in a pocket.

title: The Curiosity rover lands on Mars
blurb: It was lowered to the surface on cables from a hovering rocket-powered crane.

title: COVID-19 is declared a pandemic
blurb: Schools and borders closed around the world. Vaccines were developed faster than for any disease before.
